title: The Last Ledger Anew
premise: In the river city of Velden, 1847, Astrid Marchetti works the type cases in her father's print shop while revolution gathers beyond the windows. When census taker Ivo Kessler discovers the shop has been secretly printing pamphlets for the exiled reformer Tomas Brandt — Astrid's late mother's oldest friend, now declared an enemy of the state — he faces a choice: report them or protect a promise he made to Astrid's mother before the borders closed. As the uprising ignites and soldiers begin a door-to-door search, Astrid must smuggle Brandt's final manuscript out of the city, choosing between her family's safety and the truth her mother died believing. The book ends with the shop burned, the manuscript published abroad under her mother's name, and Astrid realizing that history was never something that happened to other people — she has been setting it, letter by letter, all along.
about_author: E. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former typesetter and archivist who spent a decade cataloguing nineteenth-century print shops in central Europe. Their debut novel was inspired by a single surviving ledger of forbidden pamphlets found sewn into the binding of a hymnal.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Introduces the Marchetti print shop, her father's fading eyesight, and her pride in the craft of setting type. She believes politics is ink wasted on paper that no one reads. Emotional beat: quiet contentment built on a fragile illusion of ordinary life.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Census taker Ivo Kessler arrives for his count, but lingers over a locked drawer of unsold pamphlets and asks about a name — Brandt — that makes her father go white. Emotional beat: the first crack in Astrid's belief that history passes them by.

chapters.title: What Mother Left in the Type Case
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Searching her mother's old sorting tray, Astrid finds letters proving her mother and Tomas Brandt were collaborators and dear friends — and that Ivo was once their ally. Emotional beat: grief rekindled, the past made suddenly dangerous.

chapters.title: The Census Taker's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Torn between duty and the promise he made Astrid's mother to protect Brandt's people, Ivo warns the Marchettis that a raid is coming, then destroys his own notes. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty begins to show on his face.

chapters.title: Pamphlets at Midnight
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Rather than burn the stock, Astrid secretly prints a new edition of Brandt's essay, her first act of open defiance. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into purpose; she belongs to something at last.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Tea
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Summoned by Magistrate Hahn, Ivo must lie to a man who knew his father, deepening his deception. A colleague suspects him. Emotional beat: loyalty to the dead pulling against survival in the living world.

chapters.title: Bread, Salt, and Rumors of War
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The city braces for the uprising; neighbors who once shunned the shop now ask quietly for pamphlets. Astrid's father collapses under the strain. Emotional beat: community crystallizing, but at a price the family cannot yet pay.

chapters.title: A Letter with No Address
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A smuggled letter from Brandt asks the Marchettis to safeguard his final manuscript — the one thing he cannot publish if caught. Astrid promises, repeating her mother's old vow. Emotional beat: a promise made in peacetime becoming a debt in wartime.

chapters.title: The First Barricade
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Revolution ignites; Ivo is ordered to help search the print district and must misdirect his own men. He passes Astrid in the smoke and says nothing. Emotional beat: complicity and courage blurring into the same act.

chapters.title: Hidden in Plain Type
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The manuscript arrives sewn into a hymnal; Astrid hides its pages as locked type forms, disguised as ordinary job work. Her father, recovering, silently helps her. Emotional beat: father and daughter reconciled through shared risk.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. An apprentice from a rival shop denounces the Marchettis; Hahn orders a full search within three days. Ivo realizes he can no longer protect them from inside. Emotional beat: dread tightening; the clock begins.

chapters.title: Three Days of Ink
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid races to print a second copy of the manuscript to send abroad, working by candlelight while soldiers drill in the square. Emotional beat: obsessive devotion; memory made physical in lead and ink.

chapters.title: What Ivo Knew About Her Mother
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confesses to Astrid the full story: her mother's arrest, the promise extracted from him on the prison steps, his years of silence. Emotional beat: betrayal and devotion revealed as the same wound.

chapters.title: The Apprentice's Price
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid confronts the informer, a boy her own age, and discovers he denounced the shop to save his imprisoned sister. Emotional beat: mercy complicating anger; enemies revealed as mirrors.

chapters.title: Doors Knocked Down
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The search begins early. Ivo falsifies the route of his squad, buying hours he knows he'll hang for. Emotional beat: the point of no return, crossed with terrible calm.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Marchetti Shop
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Soldiers torch the shop; Astrid's father is injured shielding the press, and the original manuscript burns with the building. Emotional beat: devastation; the loss of home, livelihood, and proof all at once.

chapters.title: Ashes and Locked Forms
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the rubble, Astrid realizes the second copy survives — as set type hidden in a coffin-bound consignment her father arranged years ago. Emotional beat: despair pierced by inheritance; her mother's foresight saving them again.

chapters.title: The River at Night
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo uses his census knowledge of every door and dock to guide Astrid and the type past checkpoints to a river barge bound for Basel. They are nearly caught; a young soldier dies in the confusion. Emotional beat: escape shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Hahn's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Arrested, Ivo faces Hahn, who offers leniency if he names the smugglers. Ivo refuses and is imprisoned, finally at peace with the promise kept. Emotional beat: loyalty triumphant over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Name
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In Basel, Astrid meets the dying Brandt, who asks that the manuscript be published under her mother's name, not his. Emotional beat: recognition; the promise completed and its meaning transformed.

chapters.title: Setting the Last Page
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In a foreign print shop, Astrid sets the final page herself, her mother's name in the largest type on the title page. The pamphlet spreads back across the border. Emotional beat: grief and triumph fused; memory preserved in print.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, years later. Velden has changed regimes twice; Astrid returns to rebuild the shop, visits Ivo's grave, and trains apprentices — including the former informer's sister. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a place but in the work of keeping truth legible.
